package: Johanson Manufacturing (Knowles Precision Devices) 5602, air-dielectric trimmer capacitor, panel/PCB-mount, threaded case (.234-64 UNS-2A), top screwdriver-slot adjust, one separate insulated lead wire. Overall body/hex-collar envelope dia 6.99-7.49 mm (catalog col C).
description: Johanson 5602, 1-30 pF air trimmer, 250 VDC (500 VDC test), -65 to +125 C, Q>800 @ 100 MHz. DigiKey 1956-1000-ND, Active, 373 in stock, $63.37/ea qty 1-19 (all figures re-confirmed live this pass, matching research/trimmer-cap.json and research/components.md 'Trimmer temperature re-selection' section). '5602' IS the complete orderable manufacturer part number - confirmed directly on the DigiKey product page ('Manufacturer Part Number: 5602 ... appears to be the complete orderable P/N; no suffix variants mentioned'), unlike the retired BFC2808 family which used a catalog-number/suffix scheme (BFC2 808 11339). Chosen (state.json P3 decision, 2026-08-09T00:23:01) over the electrically-similar Johanson 8052 specifically because 5602's tuning tool P/N is confirmed (8764) while 8052's is not.

pinout.name: STATOR
pinout.notes: PHYSICAL ASSIGNMENT (state.json P3 decision, 2026-08-09, supersedes the rotor/stator-inference note below): pad 1 = the case/thread/hex-collar assembly -> GND. Decided on physical/mechanical terms, not on internal rotor/stator identity: a panel-mount trimmer's case is engineered to pass through a grounded metal panel, so the case is the ground-compatible terminal by construction, and it is also the only terminal a hand or tool actually brushes during tuning - so it must be grounded regardless of which plate is electrically the rotor or the stator. 'STATOR' is kept here only as the mechanical descriptor (the case is the fixed, non-rotating structure; does not imply an electrical role) - it mounts through the board via the .234-64 UNS-2A thread and carries the top screwdriver-slot tuning access on its far face.

pinout.name: ROTOR
pinout.notes: PHYSICAL ASSIGNMENT (state.json P3 decision, 2026-08-09, supersedes the rotor/stator-inference note below): pad 2 = the separate, insulated lead wire (0.015in / 0.38mm dia, catalog Fig 3/4) -> RF. 'ROTOR' is kept here only as the mechanical descriptor (the lead is the only mechanically plausible exit path for the internally-adjusted plate's connection, since the top screwdriver slot itself cannot be a solder point) - it does not drive the net assignment, which is decided on the case-is-touchable-so-case-is-GND reasoning under pin 1 above.

land_pattern.package: 2-pad THT: one large plated hole for the threaded case/bushing, one small plated hole for the separate lead wire
land_pattern.notes: NOT a published land pattern - Johanson/Knowles do not recommend a PCB land pattern for this part (it is documented as a panel-mount part, normally through a metal chassis panel with a hex nut, not a PCB). pitch_mm (6.00mm, pad centres) is THIS LIBRARIAN'S OWN layout choice (clearance-driven: gives 1.40mm edge-to-edge copper gap between the two pads at the pad sizes chosen, comfortably above the board's 0.80mm HV floor for a 122.5 Vpeak / 101-150V-band net pair), not a transcribed catalog dimension - the catalog's own lead-offset figure (~0.09in / 2.29mm, Fig 3) could not be resolved with confidence for Fig 4 (5602's own drawing; its H/J/F/K sub-dimensions did not resolve cleanly from the scanned catalog) and in any case falls inside this footprint's larger pad's own radius, so it could not be used directly - the 0.38mm lead is flexible/hand-formable at this build's qty-5 scale, matching the project's existing 'measure and confirm at assembly' precedent for R1 (parts/T50R0-250-12X.json). pad_size_mm and drill_mm are DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the two pads have different, deliberately different sizes (7.60/6.30mm for the case, 1.60/0.80mm for the lead) so no single value describes both, and fp_verify's pad_size/drill checks apply one expected value across all copper - including either would create a false-mismatch on whichever pad does not match. Pad 1 (case): drill 6.30mm clears the .234-64 UNS-2A thread's 5.94mm nominal major diameter with ~0.18mm radial clearance for hand insertion; pad copper 7.60mm dia (>= the catalog's 7.49mm max body/hex-collar envelope, col C) lands the full shoulder for solder. Pad 2 (lead): drill 0.80mm, pad 1.60mm dia, generous for the 0.38mm wire.

layout_notes: SOURCE HIERARCHY for this extraction: (1) DigiKey product page https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/knowles-johanson-manufacturing/5602/9094387 (parametric spec table + MPN confirmation, fetched this pass), (2) Knowles combined trimmer catalog https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/6592/KnowlesTrimmersCatalogueweb177409287.pdf pp.14-17 'Air Trimmers' section, the '5600/5602' dimension-table row and Figures 3 (5600) / 4 (5602) (fetched and read at 600dpi crop this pass - this is the ONLY source with an actual mechanical drawing for this part), (3) the Johanson 'Air Capacitors' family sell sheet farnell.com/datasheets/35551.pdf (corroborates capacitance range, Q, voltage, temperature, tuning tool P/N against the combined catalog; its own per-part drawings render badly (custom-encoded font, digits reliable, prose garbled) so the combined catalog was preferred for dimensions), (4) research/components.md 'Trimmer temperature re-selection' section and research/trimmer-cap.json (prior scout pass, re-confirmed not re-derived, for temperature/voltage/stock/price/tool headline facts).

BODY/CASE (combined catalog p.17 table, row '5600 / 5602', col C, shared across both figures): overall envelope diameter 0.275-0.295in = 6.99-7.49mm. This is the widest point of the case (a round body with wrench-flats machined in for the '.28in A/F' hex feature shown in the end-view of both Fig 3 and Fig 4 - the hex corners cannot exceed the round OD they are cut into, so 7.49mm is the true, conservative overall envelope; the hex itself is a sub-feature, not the full body shape).

THREAD (combined catalog p.17 table col '(UNS-2A)', both Fig 3 and Fig 4): .234-64 UNS-2A, i.e. nominal major diameter 0.234in = 5.94mm, 64 threads/in, class 2A (external). This is the portion that passes through the panel/PCB; a separate small hex nut (0.040in / 1.02mm thick, catalog-labelled 'HEX NUT') threads onto it from the far side for panel mounting - NOT modelled/required by this footprint (this board solders the case directly into a plated hole at qty-5 scale; hardware inclusion with the DigiKey SKU could not be confirmed one way or the other this pass - open item, non-blocking since the nut is not relied on).

OVERALL LENGTH (combined catalog p.17 table, row '5600/5602', cols A + B): A=0.68in (17.3mm, case body length before the thread begins) + B=0.25in (6.35mm, threaded stub length) = approx 0.93in / 23.6mm total, before-nut. This is markedly LONGER than the retired BFC280811339's 10mm max overall height - flagged for the architect/P6 as a mechanical Z-clearance change (this part stands much taller above the board once top-mounted with the tuning slot up), even though the pad-plane (X-Y) envelope is comparable. Not independently re-verified against Fig 4's own H/J/F/K sub-dimensions (could not be resolved to certainty from the scanned catalog at the resolution available) - treat as approximate, order-of-magnitude confirmed against the neighbouring sibling 5601's own '.740in' total-length figure on the same page.

LEAD (combined catalog p.17 Fig 3, clearer of the two drawings for this dimension): diameter 0.015in = 0.38mm, insulated, exits bent at an angle near the base of the case/hex-collar, offset approximately 0.09in (2.29mm) from the body's central axis per Fig 3's end-view. Fig 4 (5602's own drawing) shows the equivalent feature but its H/J/F/K sub-dimensions did not resolve to a confirmed number from the scanned catalog image - this footprint therefore does NOT use the catalog's own offset for pad-2 placement (see land_pattern.notes).

TUNING SLOT (combined catalog p.17, both Fig 3 and Fig 4 end-views): centred on the case's far face (opposite the lead), a small recessed feature ~0.047in (1.19mm) dia shown as a hidden-line (dashed) circle inside the '.28in A/F' hex end-view, with a 'TUNING SLOT' leader. This is the only screwdriver access point.

NET ASSIGNMENT (state.json P3 decision, 2026-08-09): pad 1 (case/thread/hex-collar) -> GND, pad 2 (insulated lead) -> RF. Decided on PHYSICAL terms, not on the internal rotor/stator identity of the two plates (which remains unlabelled by every source checked - DigiKey parametric page, the combined Knowles catalog, the Johanson family sell sheet, Knowles' own 'Quick Guide to Trimmer Capacitor Selection' blog post, a Knowles/Voltronics technical note on passive-components.eu, RFMW's and Octopart's listings, and a patent/prior-art search for the 'one piece self-locking constant drive mechanism... transverse slots' construction described on the family sell sheet's p.1 - contrast the retired BFC280811339, whose datasheet explicitly printed 'R = Rotor, S = Stator'). That question no longer needs answering: a panel-mount trimmer's case is engineered to pass through a grounded metal panel, so the case is the ground-compatible terminal by construction, and the case is also the only terminal a hand or tool actually brushes during tuning - so it is the terminal that must be grounded whatever its internal role is. This makes 'exposed metal is at ground' true regardless of which plate physically moves, closing the safety question the earlier rotor/stator inference could not.

TOOL: Johanson 8764, .130in (3.30mm) shank diameter, non-metallic tip preferred - confirmed for the 52/53/54/55/56/57-series family (5602's '56' prefix matches the 5600-row) in the combined catalog's tool cross-reference table (p.2, re-cited from research/components.md; not independently re-fetched this pass since already citation-grade from the prior research pass).

ELECTRICAL (DigiKey parametric page + combined catalog p.14-17, cross-checked, consistent): capacitance range 1-30 pF (>20 turns); working voltage 250 VDC (500 VDC test); operating temperature -65 to +125 C; Q > 800 @ 100 MHz (the worst-Q member of the whole Johanson air-trimmer family, per research/components.md's whole-family sweep - the tradeoff for the wide 1-30pF span); insulation resistance > 10^6 Mohm (family sell sheet characteristics list); RoHS compliant; torque 1 to 5.0 oz-in; rotational life not separately stated for this SKU (the sibling Voltronics 'A series' on an adjacent catalog page states 10000 turns rotational life for a different, internally-sealed construction - NOT carried over to this part, different family).

SHARED-LAND-PATTERN EVALUATION (task requirement: judge honestly whether one footprint can accept both this part and the retired BFC280811339): NOT DONE, by inspection, no geometry test needed. BFC280811339 is a 3-pad THT L-pattern, 2.2mm round pads on a 1.3mm drill, legs 5.08mm. This part is a 2-pad THT design with pad 1 alone (7.60mm/6.30mm drill) already 3.5x the diameter of BFC280811339's largest pad, and a different pad COUNT (2 vs 3) and mounting mechanic (one large threaded-bushing hole vs three small leg holes). There is no common hole/pad geometry that is simultaneously small enough to solder BFC280811339's 1.3mm leads without a huge annulus/false joint and large enough to pass this part's 5.94mm thread - and BFC280811339 has no third pad position this part could use either. Shipped as two separate footprints (5602-only for the new footprint; BFC280811339's existing 3-pad footprint untouched) - no dual-fit attempted.

3D MODEL: none available. This part is DigiKey-only (not on LCSC), so lib_pull.py/easyeda2kicad has no source to pull a STEP/WRL model from, unlike the retired BFC280811339 (which has lib/aiee.3dshapes/CAP-ADJ-TH_3P-BD7.6_BFC280811339.step/.wrl from its LCSC pull). The new footprint's (model ...) block is omitted rather than left dangling. Open item for P9 (renders/CPL) if a visual model is wanted later - would need to be hand-modelled or sourced from Johanson/Knowles directly.
